answer: Delayed-Reply Queue. Each new identity must answer live queries in a serialized queue; replies are held for a copper cooling period before counting as valid. An identity that stops responding loses its queue slot, and restarting requires re-entering at the back of a spiral of accumulated backlog. The queue position acts as an anchor tying throughput to real time spent. An attacker running many identities must staff each one continuously through the cooling period; idle fakes forfeit position, so the per-identity cost is sustained attention, not a one-time fee.
